headline: Colorado edges Michigan in turnover-marred defensive slugfest
body: Colorado escaped Ann Arbor with a two-point victory in a game that felt far tighter than the final score suggests. Michigan's offense moved the ball adequately—348 yards and two touchdowns from Browne—but two costly fumbles short-circuited scoring opportunities at critical junctures. Colorado's defense, anchored by Stoutmire's five tackles, bent without breaking when it mattered most, forcing those turnovers and preventing Michigan from establishing rhythm despite nearly matching the Buffaloes in total yardage.

Roger Anderson's 267-yard passing performance earned him Player of the Game honors, though it masked an inefficient night: 22 completions on 41 attempts reflects a quarterback working through tight coverage all evening. The real difference came through Colorado's ability to cash in on Michigan's mistakes. Sweeney's rushing touchdown and Mecum's explosive 72-yard reception on just two catches gave Colorado just enough firepower to weather Michigan's sustained pressure. Browne's dual-touchdown showing and Burkett's grinding 18-carry effort kept the Wolverines in position to win, but the fumbles—one deep in the third quarter with momentum—proved unforgivable.

The final thirty seconds encapsulated the entire contest: Colorado's defense stiffened, Michigan couldn't capitalize on possession advantage, and a team that committed zero turnovers proved marginally more disciplined when discipline mattered. Neither offense dominated, neither defense was suffocating, but in a week ten matchup where field position and ball security became currency, Colorado simply managed both slightly better.
turningPoint: Michigan's second fumble with roughly twelve minutes remaining killed what appeared to be a go-ahead drive, giving Colorado the field position and momentum to engineer the game-winning sequence.

unsungHero.name: WR Mecum
unsungHero.why: Two receptions for 72 yards—a 36-yard average—means one explosive play likely went for 60-plus yards while the other converted critical yardage, yet Anderson's passing night and the overall team victory overshadow how that one catch changed Colorado's entire possession outcome.
